response: By default, tests do not expire — the Test Expiration Time fields are empty unless you explicitly set a start and end date/time. If no expiration is set, the test remains active indefinitely. Separately, each test invite can have its own Invite Expiry (duration or fixed end date), which is disabled by default.

Based on HackerRank documentation, test variants and separate tests serve different purposes:

**When to use test variants** (Document 1, 3, 5):
- Use variants when you want a single assessment that adapts to different candidate profiles (roles, skills, or other criteria).
- Variants let you personalize evaluation within one test, eliminating the need to manage separate tests, improving efficiency, and reducing maintenance overhead while providing flexibility at scale.
- Variant logic can route candidates to different variants based on their answers to a qualifying question (Document 5).
- A variant-based test requires at least two variants (Document 1).

**When to create a new test** (Document 2):
- Create a new test (custom test) when you need a highly tailored assessment for specific hiring needs—for example, a particular role, skill level, or experience (e.g., a Quality Assurance Engineer with five years of experience and expertise in test automation).
- Predefined role-based tests (like Front End Developer for React, Angular, Vue.js) are created as separate tests from the role list.

**Advantages of variants** (Document 1, 3):
- Single assessment to manage instead of multiple separate tests.
- Improves efficiency and reduces maintenance overhead.
- Ensures candidates are assessed on the most relevant content for their profile.
- Flexibility to personalize assessments at scale.
- Can reuse sections across variants via "Add from Other Variants" (Document 1).

**Disadvantages / considerations** (inferred from documentation):
- Variants require at least two variants and setup of variant logic.
- May add complexity if the assessment differences are minor or if you need completely distinct tests.
- Time adjustments for candidates can only be applied in bulk when all selected candidates belong to the same variant (Document 5).
justification: Document 1 explains test variants allow a single assessment adapting to different candidate profiles, eliminating separate test management and improving efficiency. Document 2 describes creating custom tests for highly tailored assessments. Document 3 notes variants reduce maintenance overhead while enabling personalization at scale. Document 5 adds that variant logic routes candidates based on qualifying questions and that bulk time adjustments require candidates to be in the same variant.

To give the candidate 50% extra time (≈53 minutes on a 105-minute test) and have the updated duration appear in the reinvitation email, you must first apply a **Time Accommodation** (percentage-based) and then reinvite the candidate. The "Add Time" feature (minutes-based) is for adding time during or after a test session and does not update the invitation email.

**Step-by-step:**

1. **Apply Time Accommodation (50%)**
   - Log in to HackerRank for Work.
   - Go to the **Tests** tab and open the relevant test.
   - Go to the **Candidates** tab.
   - Select the checkbox next to the candidate.
   - Click **More > Add Time Accommodation**.
   - Enter **50** (percentage, in multiples of five).
   - Click **Save**. A success message appears. The updated duration (157.5 minutes) will now show in the test invite email and on the test landing page.

2. **Reinvite the Candidate**
   - With the candidate still selected (or re-select), click **Invite selected**.
   - In the **Send Test Invites** section, click **Send invite**.
   - A confirmation appears noting the candidate has already attempted; click **Re-invite**.
   - Click **Send invite** to complete the reinvitation.

The candidate will receive a new invitation email showing the accommodated duration (≈158 minutes). If the candidate has already started the test, they must refresh the page to see the updated timer.
justification: Document 1 explains that Time Accommodation (percentage) updates the duration in the invite email and landing page, while Add Time (minutes) is for in-session adjustments and does not update the email. Document 2 provides the reinvitation procedure. Combining both gives the correct workflow.
